answer: Rotating Raven Quorum. Each agent identity must answer a fresh, context-derived challenge whose solution depends on a private seed bound to a hardware kernel at enrollment, so responses cannot be copied from another agent. A random island of reviewers cross-checks consistency across sessions. An attacker pays one distinct hardware kernel and a full enrollment delay per identity; cloning a working identity costs a new device and re-derivation, making mass duplication linear and expensive.
